name: SoLid
full_name: Search for Oscillations with a Lithium-6 Detector
summary: SoLid uses a finely segmented composite scintillator detector at the BR2 research reactor in Belgium. Its short baseline and three-dimensional event localization target sterile-neutrino disappearance and the uranium-235 antineutrino spectrum.
detection_principle: Five-centimetre PVT cubes provide the hydrogen target and positron signal. Lithium-6 fluoride/zinc-sulfide screens capture neutrons with a distinct pulse shape; wavelength-shifting fibres and silicon photomultipliers reconstruct prompt/delayed coincidences.

status.label: Status not established
status.evidence: The 2025 physics paper reports a completed analysis sample. The project report documents Phase-I running to July 2020 and Phase-II running from February 2021; its expected 2022 end date is not treated as a verified actual stop date.

timeline.event: Phase-I data taking ended and photosensor upgrade followed
Phase-II stable physics data taking began
First sterile-oscillation result released as a preprint and published in Physical Review D

key_parameters.value: Highly enriched uranium BR2 research reactor

key_parameters.name: First oscillation-analysis sample
key_parameters.value: 280 reactor-on and 172 reactor-off live days; 29,479 ± 603 statistical antineutrino candidates

results.summary: The collaboration documented the detector response, calibration and neutron/positron reconstruction needed for a sterile-neutrino analysis.
The first oscillation analysis obtained constraints from complementary frequentist and Bayesian fits. It did not establish a sterile-neutrino discovery.
